 Phoenix offers SNAP application support amid Arizona’s steep drop in enrollment 
 By Veronica Stracqualursi Published : Oct. 26, 2026 at 3:14 PM MST | Updated : 15 minutes ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google PHOENIX (AZFamily/AP) — Phoenix is offering free assistance for residents to navigate the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program, or SNAP, after Arizona saw a steep drop in enrollment amid federal cuts.
 A new city initiative provides residents with help applying, renewing and maintaining their SNAP benefits with the Arizona Department of Economic Security.
 Through the city’s SNAP Navigation Support initiative , Phoenix residents can receive one‑on‑one assistance completing their SNAP applications and submitting renewals, guidance on meeting the work requirements and post-application support.
 “Navigating the SNAP application process can be complicated, and this program ensures Phoenix families have the support they need,” Phoenix Mayor Kate Gallego said in a statement. 
 “Far too many people are losing their nutritional safety net because of federal changes, paperwork errors, and red tape. This initiative is a critical lifeline to keep children from going hungry, and supports families and seniors who are struggling with the high cost of food,” she added. 
 Residents can schedule an in-person or virtual appointment through the city’s website . In-person appointments are being offered at the three city family service centers: John F. Long Family Services Center, Sunnyslope Family Services Center and the Travis L. Williams Family Services Center. Walk-ins are also welcome.
 Residents are encouraged to bring any available documents, including identity verification, proof of address, income information for all household members, Social Security numbers, bank statements, documentation related to volunteer hours or federal workforce program participation, and any DES notices related to renewals or updates. 
 Millions of people lost their food stamps after President Donald Trump’s “One Big Beautiful Bill” took effect, requiring stricter work requirements to qualify for the federal food aid program. Arizona was the state hit the hardest , with a 12-month drop in enrollment of more than 50%. 
 Experts anticipate another blow to the SNAP program once the cost-sharing requirement of the law kicks in next October.
 The Associated Press contributed to this report.
